raw_request: User request: Update current @[app/src/api] implementation to utilize a real SQL db connection, with connection string managed by config

capability_analysis.core_action: Replace in-memory data repositories with SQL database-backed repositories while maintaining API compatibility
inputs_required: SQL database connection string from appsettings.json
outputs_expected: Properly configured ApplicationDbContext with DbSets for Account and Transaction
Dependency injection configuration in Program.cs using SQL repositories
Database schema supporting Account and Transaction entities
state_changes: Data persisted to SQL database instead of in-memory collections
Account and transaction data survives application restarts
Connection string configurable per environment via appsettings.json
side_effects: Database must be created and accessible
Seed data initialization may need to be updated to use SQL repositories
Application startup may fail if database is unavailable

system_components_affected.ui_affected: None - API only, no UI changes
system_components_affected.api_endpoints: All existing endpoints (GET/POST transactions, GET accounts) continue to work unchanged
database_changes: Create Account table with Id, AccountName, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt columns
Create Transaction table with Id, SourceAccountId, TargetAccountId, Amount, Date, CreatedAt columns
Add foreign key relationships between Transaction and Account
system_components_affected.external_services: SQL Server database (or other SQL provider configured)

acceptance_criteria_analysis.criterion: SQL repositories implement the same interfaces as in-memory repositories
acceptance_criteria_analysis.gherkin: Given the API is configured with SQL database connection, When a transaction is created via POST /api/transactions, Then it is persisted to the SQL database and retrievable via GET /api/transactions
acceptance_criteria_analysis.test_approach: Integration test: Create transaction, verify in database, retrieve via API

acceptance_criteria_analysis.criterion: Connection string is read from appsettings.json configuration
acceptance_criteria_analysis.gherkin: Given appsettings.json contains a valid SQL connection string under ConnectionStrings:DefaultConnection, When the application starts, Then it successfully connects to the specified database
acceptance_criteria_analysis.test_approach: Unit test: Verify Program.cs reads connection string from configuration

acceptance_criteria_analysis.criterion: Database context is properly registered in dependency injection
acceptance_criteria_analysis.gherkin: Given the application is configured with DbContext, When a repository is instantiated, Then it receives a valid ApplicationDbContext instance with database connectivity
acceptance_criteria_analysis.test_approach: Integration test: Verify repositories can execute queries against database

acceptance_criteria_analysis.criterion: Existing API endpoints continue to work with SQL-backed repositories
acceptance_criteria_analysis.gherkin: Given the API endpoints are unchanged, When requests are made to GET /api/transactions and POST /api/transactions, Then they correctly retrieve/persist data from/to SQL database
acceptance_criteria_analysis.test_approach: Integration tests for each endpoint with SQL backend

acceptance_criteria_analysis.criterion: Account and transaction data models are properly mapped to database entities
acceptance_criteria_analysis.gherkin: Given the Account and Transaction domain models exist, When data is persisted to SQL, Then the database schema correctly represents all properties and relationships

acceptance_criteria_analysis.criterion: Error handling for database connection failures
acceptance_criteria_analysis.gherkin: Given the database is unavailable, When the application attempts to access data, Then it returns appropriate HTTP 500 error with meaningful message

acceptance_criteria_analysis.criterion: Seed data is properly initialized in SQL database
acceptance_criteria_analysis.gherkin: Given the application starts with an empty database, When the seed data initialization runs, Then the 5 test accounts are created in the SQL database
acceptance_criteria_analysis.test_approach: Integration test: Verify accounts exist after startup
dependencies: Seed data logic updated for SQL repositories

edge_cases.case: Connection string is missing from appsettings.json
edge_cases.impact: Application startup fails or falls back to in-memory
edge_cases.handling: Validate connection string exists and is non-empty during startup

edge_cases.case: Connection string is invalid or database is unreachable
edge_cases.impact: Application cannot start or requests fail
edge_cases.handling: Provide clear error message indicating database connectivity issue

edge_cases.case: Database exists but tables do not exist
edge_cases.impact: Queries fail with table not found errors
edge_cases.handling: Implement database migrations or schema initialization on startup

edge_cases.case: Multiple application instances access the same database
edge_cases.impact: Potential race conditions or locking issues
edge_cases.handling: Ensure Entity Framework Core handles concurrent access properly with transactions

edge_cases.case: Transaction creation fails midway (e.g., database error after validation)
edge_cases.impact: Partial data state or inconsistent balance calculations
edge_cases.handling: Wrap repository operations in transactions to ensure atomicity

edge_cases.case: Seed data already exists in database on application restart
edge_cases.handling: Check if accounts exist before seeding, or use idempotent seed logic

edge_cases.case: Different connection strings needed for Development vs Production
edge_cases.impact: Wrong database accessed in different environments

existing_code: ITransactionRepository interface - must be implemented by SQL repository
IAccountRepository interface - must be implemented by SQL repository
new_code: ApplicationDbContext DbSet properties for Account and Transaction
Entity Framework Core configuration in ApplicationDbContext.OnModelCreating
infrastructure: SQL Server database (or configured SQL provider)
Entity Framework Core NuGet package (likely already present)
SQL Server provider for Entity Framework Core
external_services: SQL Server instance accessible at connection string

blocks: Any feature requiring persistent data storage

domain_knowledge: Business rules for transaction creation and balance constraints

open_questions.current_assumption: SQL Server (based on appsettings.json connection string format)

open_questions.current_assumption: Yes, seed data should be created in SQL database on startup

open_questions.question: Should database migrations be automated or manual?
open_questions.current_assumption: Automated migrations on application startup for development

open_questions.current_assumption: Based on domain models: Account (Id, AccountName, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt), Transaction (Id, SourceAccountId, TargetAccountId, Amount, Date, CreatedAt)

open_questions.question: Are there any performance or scalability requirements?

complexity_assessment.reasoning: Requires understanding of Entity Framework Core, SQL database design, and .NET dependency injection. The actual implementation is straightforward since repository interfaces are already defined and the CQRS pattern is established. Main complexity is in proper database schema design and ensuring data integrity.
risk_factors: Database connectivity issues in different environments
complexity_assessment.estimated_effort: 4-6 hours for complete implementation including testing
